bodyMarkdown:
Where the Cumberland crosses the hard Lower Pennsylvanian Rockcastle conglomerate, softer rock below erodes faster and keeps a ~68-foot, 125-foot-wide drop—the “Niagara of the South.” The falls likely began near the Pottsville Escarpment by Burnside and retreated about 45 miles upstream, cutting the gorge. On clear full-moon nights the mist throws a moonbow, the only place in the Western Hemisphere where moonbows are known to appear with regularity. T. Coleman du Pont bought the falls and surrounding land, his family donated it to Kentucky after his death, and the state park opened in 1931.
Source: [Cumberland Falls (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumberland_Falls)
Source: [Geologic Story of Kentucky (Kentucky Geological Survey)](https://kgs.uky.edu/kgsweb/olops/pub/kgs/GeoStory.pdf)
